silver_models.name: stg_customers
silver_models.description: One row per per-order customer_id; retain the person-level identity for customer analytics. Test primary key unique and not null.

silver_models.name: stg_orders
silver_models.description: One row per order, without status filtering. Test primary key unique and not null.

silver_models.name: stg_order_items
silver_models.description: One row per original order item; retain all items without aggregation. Test the composite primary key unique and each component not null.

silver_models.name: stg_reviews
silver_models.description: One row per (review_id, order_id), preserving all original reviews; omit free-text PII. Test composite primary key unique and each component not null.

silver_models.name: int_orders
silver_models.description: Grain: one row per order, retaining every status and all orders, including orders without items. LEFT JOIN stg_orders o to stg_customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id. Select order fields from o and customer_key from c. Customer key uniqueness prevents fanout; no aggregation or deduplication required. Test order_id unique and not null.

silver_models.name: int_order_lines
silver_models.description: Grain: one row per original order item, keyed by (order_id, order_item_id). LEFT JOIN stg_order_items i to int_orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id; select item fields from i and status, purchase timestamp, and person-level customer_key from o. Do not join payments or reviews, aggregate, filter statuses, or fabricate items for itemless orders. Test composite primary key unique and both components not null.

silver_models.name: int_order_reviews
silver_models.description: Grain: one latest review per reviewed order. Rank stg_reviews by ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY answered_at DESC NULLS LAST, review_id DESC), retain rank 1, then LEFT JOIN stg_orders on order_id for purchased_at. Return only reviewed orders; do not fabricate reviews. Test order_id unique and not null.

kpis.reason: No session or visit records exist; orders alone cannot supply the session denominator or attribute purchases to sessions.

missing: Session identifier and session start timestamp
Purchase conversion flag or order-to-session attribution
typical_sources: Web or app analytics event exports
gap.next_step: Load a session-grain dataset with session start time and a purchase conversion indicator, or events and order attribution sufficient to derive it.

kpis.reason: Item prices and freight are available, but no product unit cost or cost-of-goods-sold data is present. Sale price and freight are not substitutes for cost.

missing: Product-keyed unit cost in the sales currency
gap.next_step: Load product unit costs keyed by product_id, with currency and effective dates if costs vary; retain product_id from raw order items in silver and join the appropriate costs.

assumptions: Valid sales are orders whose normalized status is neither 'canceled' nor 'unavailable'; delivered means status exactly 'delivered'. No payment-based qualification is added.

customer_unique_id identifies a person across orders; customer_id is only the order-specific customer reference. Person identifiers remain tagged PII in silver and are used internally for aggregation only, never exposed in gold outputs.

Profile candidate business keys are trusted; unexpected duplicate or null primary keys fail tests rather than being silently discarded. Composite keys receive combination-uniqueness and component-not-null tests.
Latest review means greatest review_answer_timestamp per order; ties use descending review_id deterministically. All original reviews remain in staging.
Source timestamps are treated as timezone-unspecified timestamps with no timezone conversion; empty strings become null. Prices and freight are numeric values assumed to share one source currency.
Delivery timeliness uses calendar-day comparison and excludes delivered orders missing either delivery date from the denominator, as required by the catalogue.
Net revenue and historical CLV are revenue-based, exclude freight, and use delivered item prices without inventing discounts, refunds, taxes, or costs.

Item-based catalogue metrics operate on observed order items; itemless orders remain in int_orders for order-level metrics. Historical CLV's single item-grain template can identify first valid purchases only among orders with items; using it assumes each customer's first valid order is represented in order items. Validate this condition before approval; otherwise the CLV template needs an additional order-grain input.

Retention cohorts use the first observed valid order in the available dataset, not necessarily the customer's lifetime first order. The catalogue's last-observed-month incomplete flag is retained; no completeness beyond the observation period is assumed.

Only raw tables needed by buildable KPIs are staged; selected orders, customers, items, and reviews retain nonaggregated records. Unused PII, payments, products, sellers, translations, and geolocation are omitted.
Gold outputs contain aggregates only, with owners assigned by the selected sales, delivery, and customers domains and descriptions taken from the catalogue.
